ENIX is being constructed at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) to study the properties of extremely hot and dense matter formed in high-energy collisions. Two layers will be made of high precision sensors, two of low precision sensors, and two of high precision sensors, all connected to a common readout system. The low precision sensors will be used for tracking and the high precision sensors will be used for identifying particles. The high precision sensors will be further divided into two sub-layers, with one of them being a dedicated dedicated to measuring muons. The experiment's vertex tracker system will be able to track particles with a momentum of 0.15-100 GeV/c and will have a position resolution of 20 microns.

To counter this vulnerability, we propose a novel approach that integrates a gradient protection mechanism with the existing multi-agent reinforcement learning method. The PMADPG approach is evaluated using a simulation-based smart grid energy market model, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in protecting the gradient against the attack.

The system's behavior is examined through the lens of the Landau level, with the consideration of the effects of the vector potential on the system's topological properties. The results show that the system remains a topological insulator even at the Landau level, with the possibility of a transition occurring when the vector potential's phase factor reaches a specific value. The study also explores the effects of the vector potential on the system's transport properties, with the results indicating that the system's conductivity remains finite and independent of the Landau level index.
